newsitem.title: USA: Florida couple wins $13,000 in fingertip lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Florida couple wins $13,000 in fingertip lawsuit.

text.p: A Florida jury has awarded $13,000 to a Tampa couple who found a human fingertip in the sliced ham they bought at a Publix Supermarket.
In its verdict on Thursday, the Hillsborough County Circuit Court jury awarded David Dean $12,000 for pain, suffering and medical and psychological expenses. His wife, Katie Dean, was awarded $1,000.
David Dean found the bloody middle finger pad in July 1995 as he was ate a sandwich made from the ham his wife bought at a Tampa Publix.
Publix acknowledged that the fingertip came from an employee.

The Deans had sought $15,000 in damages for mental anguish, medical expenses for AIDS and hepatitis tests, loss of earning capacity, loss of comfort and attention of each other, and loss of "the joy of living."

The Deans and the Publix worker who cut off her fingertip tested negative for AIDS. Circuit Judge James Moody Jr. ordered the jury not to consider the fear of AIDS contraction in its verdict, citing a lack of scientific precedent.
A Publix spokeswoman said: "We feel the jury made a fair decision after evaluating this claim."
